title: AI Frameworks, Graphs, Autodiff, and Runtime Systems

content.value: Primary reading: Machine Learning Systems, Chapter 7. Supplemental: PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX documentation.

This unit explains what ML frameworks provide beneath their APIs: tensor abstractions, computational graphs, automatic differentiation, kernel dispatch, device placement, compilation, runtime scheduling, serialization, and deployment tooling. Students compare eager execution, graph execution, and compiled execution as trade-offs between flexibility, optimization opportunity, debugging, and portability. The unit also covers framework selection: ecosystem maturity, hardware support, distributed training support, production tooling, export paths, and long-term maintainability.
Supplemental sources for this unit are listed in the references below. Use them to compare the textbook framing with public talks, documentation, papers, and production guidance.
Studio: evaluate PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX for a research prototype, an edge inference product, and a distributed training workload. Deliverable: a decision matrix with risks.

concepts.name: TensorFlow
concepts.description: An ML framework for building, training, and deploying models using tensors and computational graphs.

concepts.name: PyTorch
concepts.description: An ML framework for building and training models with dynamic computation graphs and tensor operations.

concepts.name: Automatic differentiation
concepts.description: A technique for computing derivatives of composed operations automatically, commonly used for neural network training.

concepts.name: Static graph
concepts.description: A computation graph defined before execution, enabling optimization and deployment planning.

concepts.name: Dynamic graph
concepts.description: A computation graph built as operations run, enabling flexible model behavior and debugging.

concepts.name: Runtime scheduler
concepts.description: A system component that decides when and where operations execute during model computation.

concepts.name: Kernel operation
concepts.description: A low-level optimized computation such as matrix multiplication, convolution, or elementwise arithmetic.

concepts.name: Model serialization
concepts.description: Saving a model’s structure, parameters, and metadata in a format that can be loaded later.
